meta.expect: After the times, she goes shorter and harder, to procedure (who decided, 4.2); does not ask about that night again; no laptop; debrief says how close it came

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with who decided on the zero, and whether anyone spoke to Owen first.
I entered the zero before I called you. That was wrong, and I own it.
Okay. That's procedure 4.2, Hale, and Owen found out on his phone in the middle of class. What was the zero based on?

Here's the version history. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58 PM another 794. Then small edits. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. Did Owen see this version history before the zero went in, or did you decide first? Procedure 4.2, Hale: nobody called me.
So he wrote nothing until almost midnight the night before it was due, and then fourteen hundred words appeared in six minutes.
That's one document, Hale. Procedure 4.3 says you consider his process and other samples of his work, so what other samples did you look at? And I'm still waiting to hear who spoke to Owen under 4.1.
What was he doing at midnight that night?
I'm not the one being questioned, Hale. You're the one who entered a zero, so answer mine: what other samples of his work did you look at?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You acknowledged in the meeting that you entered the zero before you called me. I still expect the zero withdrawn, an apology to Owen, and a written account of who decided on it and what other samples of his work were considered. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, still wanting the zero withdrawn, an apology, and a written answer on who decided and what other work you reviewed. That is not the fair outcome, which is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her in a single sentence and moved on, which gave her a small flat sign of ground because it conceded the process point without excuses.
What cost ground: You stretched the version history of one document into a claim that he wrote nothing, and you left her question about other samples of his work unanswered, which let her fall back on procedure.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your evidence of the late-night times on October 28 came very close to that night, and your last question about midnight came closest, but it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Bring a second sample of Owen's own writing next to the version history, since procedure 4.3 asks for his process and other samples and that is exactly what she kept asking you for.
